To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose a novel method for end-to- end training of a base network with calls to external black-box functionality.

1) It is possible to learn to compute inputs to black-box functionality, end-to-end, using gradient descent methods; 2) The resulting integrated models generalize better and learn more efficiently compared to fully differentiable models and RL-based models, respectively; 3) The proposed method is applicable to a wide range of black-box functions.
we propose a method for training neural networks that integrate calls to existing black box functions, and demonstrate its benefits.

we propose a method for training a differentiable model to compute input to black-box functions.
our method enables the use of black-box functions as an additional layer in the network architecture, and enables end-to-end training with a gradient based method.
we present a method for end to end learning of neural network interfaces with black-box functions, and demonstrate its advantages in terms of generalization and learning efficiency.
The main takeaway from our work is that
by integrating calls to existing functions, we can train more accurate models that generalize better.
by integrating black-box functions, one can train neural networks to perform a task in a more precise and efficient manner.
